candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — Montenegrin bank & regulator domains
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegrin bank and regulator sites rotate/delete PDFs; Wayback is the only route to historic IR pages, annual report PDFs and press releases that were removed from cbcg.me, ckb.me, nlb.me, erstebank.me, hipotekarnabanka.com.
candidates.legal_status: public archive, ToS permits research use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CDX API (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=<domain>/*&output=json&filter=mimetype:application/pdf) to enumerate historic PDF captures, then fetch snapshots; rate-limit politely
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles archive category + snowball from bank domains found in search
queries_used: Crna Gora banka godišnji izvještaj PDF arhiva web archive CKB NLB Erste

candidates.source_name: Archive.today (archive.ph) — snapshots of ME bank/press pages
candidates.why_relevant: Complements Wayback for JS-heavy or robots-excluded Montenegrin bank pages and news items; often holds captures Wayback lacks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: manual/browser-assisted lookup per URL; no stable API
queries_used: Crna Gora banka godišnji izvještaj PDF arhiva web archive CKB NLB Erste
candidates.observed_blocker: Cloudflare interstitial commonly reported on archive.today; unverified this run

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Finansijski izvještaji banaka (bank financial statements repository)
candidates.why_relevant: Central bank acts as de-facto aggregator/archive of every licensed ME bank's audited annual financial statements, including banks whose own sites dropped the PDFs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: crawl page tree, harvest PDF links per bank per year; mirror to local store because CBCG reorganises paths
queries_used: Crna Gora banka godišnji izvještaj PDF arhiva web archive CKB NLB Erste

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Publikacije / Arhiva (publication archive)
candidates.why_relevant: Time-series of Financial Stability Reports, macro bulletins and annual reports back to ~2006; the normalising source for sector aggregates against which individual bank disclosures can be verified.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: scheduled crawl of /publikacije and /arhiva paths; diff against prior snapshot to catch silent removals
queries_used: Crna Gora banka godišnji izvještaj PDF arhiva

candidates.source_name: Portal otvorenih podataka Crne Gore (Montenegro Open Data Portal)
candidates.why_relevant: Government open-data portal with a 'Finansije' category; machine-readable datasets from ministries and agencies, an alternative durable channel when institutional HTML pages rotate.
candidates.legal_status: open government data licence (verify per dataset)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: enumerate datasets in the Finansije category; if CKAN/DKAN backed, use its API for incremental harvest
queries_used: otvoreni podaci Crna Gora portal data.gov.me finansije

candidates.source_name: eUprava Crne Gore (e-government service portal)
candidates.why_relevant: Directory of official electronic services incl. CRPS registry and financial-statement filing/access services; pointer to where structured company data actually lives.
candidates.access_status: open browsing; some services require eID
candidates.suggested_collection_method: one-off manual mapping of relevant service IDs; not a recurring crawl target
queries_used: Crna Gora CRPS registar privrednih subjekata finansijski iskazi Poreska uprava objavljivanje

candidates.source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (Uprava prihoda i carina)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory company registry: ownership, statutes, filings for banks and payment institutions; the authoritative identity/actor layer behind any disclosure time series.
candidates.access_status: search open; document copies require a request and EUR 5 fee (Art. 324 Zakon o privrednim društvima)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: targeted search per legal entity name/PIB; manual document requests for key institutions only
queries_used: Crna Gora CRPS registar privrednih subjekata finansijski iskazi Poreska uprava objavljivanje

candidates.why_relevant: Listed ME banks (e.g. Hipotekarna banka) file annual/semi-annual/quarterly reports and material-event notices with the exchange; an independent archive of the same filings banks post on IR pages.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: crawl issuer pages and news/disclosure feed; mirror PDFs

candidates.why_relevant: Third-party normaliser of Montenegroberza listings and historical instrument prices; useful cross-check and continuity when the exchange's own archive is reorganised.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: monitor the annual EU sovereign release calendar PDF and the Montenegro issuer page; capture press-release headline/date/rating, not report body

candidates.why_relevant: Fitch and Scope both maintain ME sovereign coverage with scheduled review dates; rating commentary is a compact, dated, independent read on banking-sector and fiscal conditions.

negative_findings.description: The canonical hostname of Montenegro's open data portal could not be confirmed. Searches surfaced gov.me articles announcing a new 'Open Data Portal' but returned Croatia's data.gov.hr rather than a working data.gov.me; no ME portal landing URL was directly observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: gov.me announcement pages found; portal hostname unverified (data.gov.me is a hypothesis, not a finding).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Open-data portal is the main machine-readable alternative to rotating institutional PDFs; without the right host, dataset harvesting cannot be automated.

negative_findings.description: No domestic or sr-language credit-rating agency covering Montenegrin banks was found. Searches on 'agencija za rejting Crna Gora banka ocjena izvještaj' returned no national CRA; ME coverage appears to come solely from international agencies publishing in English.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ME-domiciled or sr-language CRA identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: All rating-based verification for ME banks depends on paywalled English-language international agencies, raising cost and access risk.

negative_findings.description: No public S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating was found for individual Montenegrin banks (CKB, Hipotekarna banka, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Podgorica). Coverage found was sovereign-level plus parent-group level.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank-level ME ratings not evidenced in open sources this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank-level credit opinions may simply not exist for ME subsidiaries; collection design should rely on parent-group reports and CBCG supervisory data instead.

negative_findings.description: Montenegroberza's issuer-disclosure archive structure was not directly observed; the exchange URL was inferred from third-party references (SeeCapitalMarkets) rather than fetched.
negative_findings.result_summary: Exchange as a disclosure archive is a strong hypothesis, unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the exchange keeps a durable filings archive it is the single best non-web-archive fallback for listed ME banks.

coverage_gaps.description: Wayback coverage depth for individual ME bank domains (ckb.me, nlb.me, hipotekarnabanka.com, lovcenbanka.me, adriaticbank.com, universalcapitalbank.me, prvabankacg.com) was not enumerated in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the Wayback CDX API per bank domain filtered to PDFs, and count captures per year to identify which banks have gaps needing active Save-Page-Now capture.

coverage_gaps.description: No national digital library / legal-deposit web archive for Montenegro was searched (analogous to national library web archiving programmes elsewhere).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'Nacionalna biblioteka Crne Gore Đurđe Crnojević web arhiva / digitalna biblioteka' and check for a legal-deposit web archive covering .me domains.

coverage_gaps.description: EU/ECB-level aggregators (ECB Data Portal, EBA risk dashboards, Eurostat, EBRD/World Bank Global Findex and country diagnostics) were not enumerated for ME banking coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass over ECB Data Portal, EBRD and World Bank country datasets to find normalised ME banking/payments series.

coverage_gaps.description: The most authoritative independent commentary (Moody's, S&P, Fitch, Scope, EMIS, Cbonds) is registration- or subscription-gated, so no verified full-text collection method exists without procurement.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide licensing budget; meanwhile rely on free ratings aggregators (countryeconomy, FXEmpire) plus agency press-release headlines for event detection.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin sources exist in both Latin and Cyrillic script and under both 'crnogorski' and 'srpski' labelling; only Latin-script sr queries were run this session.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat key queries in Cyrillic ('годишњи извјештај банка Црна Гора') to catch differently-indexed archives.

brief: For Montenegro, the archive/aggregator layer is unusually load-bearing: individual bank IR pages are shallow and volatile, so the durable copies of historic disclosures sit either with the regulator (CBCG's 'Finansijski izvještaji banaka' and publication archive, which itself reorganises paths) or in the Internet Archive, making Wayback CDX enumeration plus active Save-Page-Now capture the core collection tactic. Independent normalisation comes mainly from outside the country — IMF Article IV/FSI tables, EMIS and TheBanks.eu for bank financials, and the international rating agencies for the sovereign — nearly all of the commercial ones behind registration or subscription, with free ratings aggregators (countryeconomy, FXEmpire, TheGlobalEconomy) serving as the practical event-detection substitute. Domestically, a government open-data portal with a 'Finansije' category exists but its canonical host is unconfirmed, and the CRPS company registry is search-open yet fee-gated for documents. No Montenegrin-domiciled rating agency and no public bank-level ratings for ME subsidiaries were found, so sector verification must lean on CBCG supervisory aggregates and parent-group disclosures.
